item.title: Russia backs tax rises as 2027 budget sees military spending soar
item.description:
Russia backs tax rises as 2027 budget sees military spending soar
Russia’s lower house of parliament has approved a 2027-2029 state budget and passed tax increases to fund the war in UkraineByKATIE MARIE DAVIES Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 11:12 AM
Russia’s lower house of parliament approved a 2027-2029 state budget Tuesday and separately passed a series of tax increases to fund Moscow’s war in Ukraine.
The budget allocates approximately 17.15 trillion rubles ($208.9 billion) for national defense in 2027, up from the 12.93 trillion rubles ($157.5 billion) in 2026. The amount is also a marked increase from the 13.6 trillion rubles ($165.7 billion) forecast for expenditure in 2027 in last year’s budget.
The government seeks to help cover rising military costs with additional taxes on mining companies and income from citizens’ investments.
Deputies approved the bill with 396 votes in favor and 37 abstentions. It now goes to the Federation Council, Russia’s upper house of parliament, for approval.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has increasingly sought to squeeze tax revenue out of businesses and consumers to support his nearly five-year war in Ukraine, even as the country’s economy increasingly skews toward military spending at the expense of civilian needs.
Russia’s budget deficit has swelled beyond forecast this year because of heavy military spending and sluggish economic growth. The economy has also been strained by sanctions, high interest rates for nonmilitary companies, labor shortages and Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries and export terminals.
Dmitry Kobylkin, head of the parliamentary faction for the ruling United Russia party, hailed the bill as a “victory budget,” writing in a statement that it included spending on national defense and care for veterans and their families, as well as state social support.

item.title: Gisèle Pelicot condemns publisher for using nude images from her rape case in book promo
item.description:
Gisèle Pelicot condemns publisher for using nude images from her rape case in book promo
Gisèle Pelicot says she is shocked that a Paris publisher used nude images taken by her rapist ex-husband to promote a book about her caseByJOHN LEICESTER Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 11:02 AM
PARIS -- Gisèle Pelicot says she is deeply shocked that a Paris publishing house used nude images taken of her by her rapist ex-husband as promotional materials for a book that examines her watershed fight for justice.
The 73-year-old Pelicot became an icon of courage and feminist causes during the drugging-and-rape trial in 2024 that convicted all 51 of the accused men, including her ex-husband, Dominique Pelicot.
In a statement to BFMTV, Gisèle Pelicot denounced the book, “Emprises,” and the publisher’s use of intimate photos in promoting it. The broadcaster published extracts of the statement on Monday.
“I am deeply shocked that images of the most private aspects of my life could be exhibited and exploited for commercial gain," the statement said, according to BFMTV. “I refuse to let my private life be used as a selling point."
The nude images of Pelicot were apparently taken by Dominique Pelicot and were part of the court case that saw him sentenced to 20 years in prison, said Christophe Bigot, a lawyer for Gisèle Pelicot, speaking Tuesday to The Associated Press.
Bigot said he has seen the images and that they show Gisèle Pelicot alone, without the men convicted for rapes and sexual assaults while she was unconscious, knocked out with drugs that Dominique Pelicot slipped into her food and drink.
Gisèle Pelicot's statement also criticized the book itself, saying it “describes scenes of me being raped and gives an interpretation of my life that is unbearable.”
“Above all, I refuse to let my story be re-written to suggest that I was complicit with what I was subjected to,” she said, according to the statement extracts.

item.title: South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to travel to Russia to fight against Ukraine
item.description:
South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to travel to Russia to fight against Ukraine
A Zimbabwean man has been convicted in South Africa of trying to travel to Russia to fight in its war against UkraineByMOGOMOTSI MAGOME Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 10:50 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
JOHANNESBURG -- A Zimbabwean man was convicted and sentenced on Tuesday for trying to travel to Russia to fight in its war against Ukraine after being arrested in South Africa with eight others earlier this month.
Tafadzwa Sithole was sentenced to five years in prison, suspended for five years, and he is set to be deported back to Zimbabwe.
He told a South African court that he had agreed to fight for Russia in the war in exchange for “remuneration” after successfully applying online in Zimbabwe.
Sithole said a person he identified as “Albina” contacted him after he submitted the application, arranged accommodation in South Africa and provided a flight ticket to Russia.
His admissions were detailed in a plea agreement with South African prosecutors. He pleaded guilty to violating the Regulation of Foreign Military Assistance Act, which prohibits mercenary activity and regulates military assistance to parties in foreign conflicts, including recruitment and training.
The law also applies to foreign nationals.
Sithole, who described himself as an unemployed third-year student at a university in Zimbabwe, appeared in court with four other accused who are also negotiating plea agreements with prosecutors.
He said he entered South Africa legally on Nov. 4 and stayed in accommodation in Kempton Park, east of Johannesburg, in preparation for his travel to Russia.
He was arrested at O.R. Tambo International Airport on Nov. 8 while attempting to board a flight to Russia.

item.title: Car bomb in central Colombian city injures 23 as violence spreads to urban areas
item.description:
Car bomb in central Colombian city injures 23 as violence spreads to urban areas
A bomb exploded outside regional government offices in Villavicencio, Colombia, injuring 23 peopleByMANUEL RUEDA Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 10:20 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BOGOTA, Colombia -- A bomb exploded outside regional government offices in the Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring 23 people, authorities said Tuesday, as a wave of violence involving rebel groups and drug gangs spreads to urban areas.
The explosion occurred Monday night in Villavicencio, a city with a population of half a million people. Authorities initially reported 19 injuries before raising the toll to 23. They said the attack remained under investigation.
During the first three months of his term, President Abelardo de la Espriella has increased the use of air strikes against drug gangs and rebel groups in rural areas and acted on military intelligence to capture several midlevel commanders.
Rebel groups have responded with drone attacks on police stations and military bases around the country, and have also attacked their targets with rockets made from gas cylinders and by detonating roadside bombs.
Villavicencio is a major agricultural and commercial hub on the edge of the Amazon rainforest, where rebel groups have long fought over control of drug trafficking routes, as well as legal businesses like cattle ranches and palm plantations.

item.title: Dozens killed in latest land dispute attacks in Nigeria's Niger state
item.description:
Dozens killed in latest land dispute attacks in Nigeria's Niger state
Dozens of people were killed in attacks in north-central Nigeria, advocacy groups and local authorities saidByDYEPKAZAH SHIBAYAN Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 8:22 AM
Share
ABUJA, Nigeria -- Dozens of people were killed in attacks on communities in north-central Nigeria, advocacy groups and local authorities said, in the latest violence linked to longstanding disputes between herders and farmers over grazing land and other resources.
The Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association of Nigeria, or MACBAN, which represents mostly herders from the predominantly Muslim Fulani ethnic group, said that 64 people from Fulani communities were killed over the weekend in the Borgu area of Niger state.
“The tragic incident, which reportedly claimed the lives of men, women, children and elderly persons, is a painful and devastating loss,” MACBAN special assistant Yusuf Abubakar said in a statement Monday. He called for an investigation to “bring the perpetrators to justice.”
Amnesty International Nigeria said it had obtained videos and images showing “children lined up and slaughtered, one by one, while their mothers and fathers lay in the pool of their own blood.”
Amnesty said the raid was believed to have been a reprisal for an earlier attack on Saturday.
The state’s information commissioner, Obed Nuhu Nana, said an attack on the Lumma Ba’are community in the Borgu area early Saturday left five people dead, including the village head. Five others were injured and taken to hospital, and some houses were reportedly set ablaze, Nana said in a statement.
Local resident Hassan Kafobe Dodo said Lumma Ba’are residents “assumed” the attackers who killed their village head were Fulani.

item.title: Thousands of Sikh pilgrims flood Pakistan shrine for founder of Sikhism's birthday
item.description:
Thousands of Sikh pilgrims flood Pakistan shrine for founder of Sikhism's birthday
Thousands of Sikh pilgrims from India have gathered in eastern Pakistan to celebrate the 557th birthday of Guru Nanak, the founder of SikhismByThe Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 7:40 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
NANKANA SAHIB, Pakistan -- NANKANA SAHIB, Pakistan (AP) — Thousands of Sikh pilgrims from neighboring India gathered in eastern Pakistan on Tuesday to celebrate the 557th birthday of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, officials said.
More than 5,000 worshippers attended ceremonies at a shrine in Nankana Sahib, a town in Punjab province where Guru Nanak was born. According to a government statement, Pakistan has issued visas to more than 3,000 Indian Sikhs for the occasion.
Dressed in orange, blue, yellow, and white, pilgrims filled the shrine complex with color. Men covering their heads with turbans and women with scarves, offered prayers and sang devotional hymns.

item.title: China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
item.description:
China investigates Politburo member and Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
The Chinese Communist Party is investigating Chen Jining, the CCP's secretary in Shanghai, in connection with violating party discipline, state broadcaster CCTV reportedByHUIZHONG WU Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 7:22 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BANGKOK -- Chinese Communist Party authorities are investigating Shanghai party secretary Chen Jining for suspected violations of party discipline, state media reported Tuesday.
The Politburo member is the latest senior official targeted in President Xi Jinping’s long-running anti-corruption campaign, which has shown no signs of letting up in scope or depth.
Chen is under investigation by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. The brief announcement provided no further details.
The investigation follows sweeping purges under Xi, who has emphasized greater party discipline. The Chinese leader has pursued an anti-corruption campaign for more than a decade, carrying out purges on a scale not seen since Mao Zedong’s rule.
“The takedown again shows that Xi Jinping’s anti-corruption campaign has no limits,” Mingda Qiu, a senior analyst at Eurasia Group, said in an emailed statement. “This is the fourth Politburo member to fall, and the fourth sitting member brought down in the current cycle. The pattern is unprecedented.”

item.title: British officials warn UK firms aiding Ukraine to brace for Russian sabotage threats
item.description:
British officials warn UK firms aiding Ukraine to brace for Russian sabotage threats
British security officials have warned U.K. companies supporting Ukraine's military to brace for potential sabotage attempts by RussiaByJILL LAWLESS Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 7:08 AM
LONDON -- British security officials on Tuesday warned U.K. companies supporting Ukraine’s military to brace for potential sabotage attempts by Russia.
The rare public alert came after a series of attacks and attempted attacks across Europe, amid warnings from European officials about Moscow’s hybrid attacks on digital and physical infrastructure.
Estonian authorities have said that Russia’s security services were behind an August arson attack on a defense company that provides military vehicles to Ukraine.
Estonia will close all its border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1 after authorities disrupted another attack on a defense company. Eight Latvian citizens were detained on suspicion of arson, which was ordered by Russian military intelligence, the Estonian and Latvian domestic security services said.
A U.K. court also convicted several men over a 2024 plot to set fire to a London warehouse that contained supplies for Kyiv. In September, a British man was charged with plotting with Russian spies to sabotage a drone factory, and an American soldier at a base in England was arrested earlier this month on suspicion of spying for Russia.
Authorities in Poland, Romania and other NATO countries also say they have disrupted multiple Moscow-backed sabotage plots.
The National Protective Security Authority, part of Britain’s MI5 domestic security service, and the Defense Ministry told firms providing “material support” to Ukraine’s armed forces that they may be a target for Moscow.
Chief executives from defense and critical infrastructure companies were being briefed privately by government ministers, the Defense Ministry said.

item.title: Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
item.description:
Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the country plans to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next monthByThe Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 4:45 AM
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia -- Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.
Myanmar’s government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.
Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.
He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.
Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Anwar said.
A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on Sept. 29, he said.

item.title: Serbian police arrest a 17-year-old after shots fired at a high school
item.description:
Serbian police arrest a 17-year-old after shots fired at a high school
Police in central Serbia have arrested a teenager after he fired a small-caliber rifle in a high school hallwayByThe Associated PressNovember 24, 2026, 4:27 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BELGRADE, Serbia -- Police arrested a teenager in central Serbia on Tuesday after a small-caliber rifle was fired in a high school hallway, injuring two women, authorities said.
The shooting happened around 8 a.m. at the First Technical School in Kragujevac.
Police said the teenager fired at an office near the entrance, shattering the glass and injuring two women inside. A 50-year-old woman suffered a gunshot wound to the leg, while the other was injured by flying glass.
Police later arrested the teenager’s father on suspicion of illegally possessing a weapon linked to the incident.
The women were taken to a local hospital, where doctors said their injuries were not life-threatening.

“This happened during the first class, so other students were inside the classrooms, which is good under the circumstances,” he said.
School shootings are rare in Serbia. The country’s first school shooting occurred in 2023, when a 13-year-old boy killed nine children and a school guard at an elementary school in Belgrade and injured six others.
